sanskrit.deva:
अन्यच्छ्रेयोऽन्यदुतैव प्रेयस्ते उभे नानार्थे पुरुषं सिनीतः ।
तयोः श्रेय आददानस्य साधु भवति हीयतेऽर्थाद्य उ प्रेयो वृणीते ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
anyacchreyo 'nyad utaiva preyas te ubhe nānārthe puruṣaṃ sinītaḥ |
tayoḥ śreya ādadānasya sādhu bhavati hīyate 'rthād ya u preyo vṛṇīte || 1 ||

lines.iast: anyacchreyo 'nyad utaiva preyas te ubhe nānārthe puruṣaṃ sinītaḥ
lines.deva: अन्यच्छ्रेयोऽन्यदुतैव प्रेयस्ते उभे नानार्थे पुरुषं सिनीतः

lines.iast: tayoḥ śreya ādadānasya sādhu bhavati hīyate 'rthād ya u preyo vṛṇīte
lines.deva: तयोः श्रेय आददानस्य साधु भवति हीयतेऽर्थाद्य उ प्रेयो वृणीते

padaccheda.iast: anyat śreyaḥ anyat uta eva preyaḥ te ubhe nānā-arthe puruṣam sinītaḥ tayoḥ śreyaḥ ādadānasya sādhu bhavati hīyate arthāt yaḥ u preyaḥ vṛṇīte
padaccheda.deva: अन्यत् श्रेयः अन्यत् उत एव प्रेयः ते उभे नाना-अर्थे पुरुषम् सिनीतः तयोः श्रेयः आददानस्य साधु भवति हीयते अर्थात् यः उ प्रेयः वृणीते

translations.text: “The good is one thing, and the pleasant quite another. Both, having different ends, bind a person. Of the two, it goes well with him who takes up the good; he who chooses the pleasant falls away from the goal.”

notes: Śaṅkara: Yama speaks. śreyas is the highest good (niḥśreyasa), preyas what is more pleasing. Being of the nature of knowledge and of ignorance, the two cannot be followed together by one person. The ‘goal’ is the true and lasting end of man.

sanskrit.deva:
श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतस्तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीरः ।
श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभि प्रेयसो वृणीते प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद्वृणीते ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śreyaś ca preyaś ca manuṣyam etas tau samparītya vivinakti dhīraḥ |
śreyo hi dhīro 'bhi preyaso vṛṇīte preyo mando yogakṣemād vṛṇīte || 2 ||

lines.iast: śreyaś ca preyaś ca manuṣyam etas tau samparītya vivinakti dhīraḥ
lines.deva: श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतस्तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीरः

lines.iast: śreyo hi dhīro 'bhi preyaso vṛṇīte preyo mando yogakṣemād vṛṇīte
lines.deva: श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभि प्रेयसो वृणीते प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद्वृणीते

padaccheda.iast: śreyaḥ ca preyaḥ ca manuṣyam etaḥ tau samparītya vivinakti dhīraḥ śreyaḥ hi dhīraḥ abhi preyasaḥ vṛṇīte preyaḥ mandaḥ yogakṣemāt vṛṇīte
padaccheda.deva: श्रेयः च प्रेयः च मनुष्यम् एतः तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीरः श्रेयः हि धीरः अभि प्रेयसः वृणीते प्रेयः मन्दः योगक्षेमात् वृणीते

words.meaning: for the sake of getting and keeping

translations.text: “Both the good and the pleasant come to a man. The wise one examines them well and tells them apart. The wise chooses the good over the pleasant; the dull chooses the pleasant, for the sake of getting and keeping.”

notes: abhi … vṛṇīte is one verb (abhivṛṇīte), its parts separated in the verse.

Śaṅkara: the two come as though mixed together, hard for a dull mind to separate; the wise separates them as a swan separates milk from water. yogakṣema: the increase and protection of the body and the like. The pleasant is cattle, sons and so on.

sanskrit.deva:
स त्वं प्रियान्प्रियरूपांश्च कामानभिध्यायन्नचिकेतोऽत्यस्राक्षीः ।
नैतां सृङ्कां वित्तमयीमवाप्तो यस्यां मज्जन्ति बहवो मनुष्याः ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sa tvaṃ priyān priyarūpāṃś ca kāmān abhidhyāyan naciketo 'tyasrākṣīḥ |
naitāṃ sṛṅkāṃ vittamayīm avāpto yasyāṃ majjanti bahavo manuṣyāḥ || 3 ||

lines.iast: sa tvaṃ priyān priyarūpāṃś ca kāmān abhidhyāyan naciketo 'tyasrākṣīḥ
lines.deva: स त्वं प्रियान्प्रियरूपांश्च कामानभिध्यायन्नचिकेतोऽत्यस्राक्षीः

lines.iast: naitāṃ sṛṅkāṃ vittamayīm avāpto yasyāṃ majjanti bahavo manuṣyāḥ
lines.deva: नैतां सृङ्कां वित्तमयीमवाप्तो यस्यां मज्जन्ति बहवो मनुष्याः

padaccheda.iast: saḥ tvam priyān priya-rūpān ca kāmān abhidhyāyan naciketaḥ atyasrākṣīḥ na etām sṛṅkām vitta-mayīm avāptaḥ yasyām majjanti bahavaḥ manuṣyāḥ
padaccheda.deva: सः त्वम् प्रियान् प्रिय-रूपान् च कामान् अभिध्यायन् नचिकेतः अत्यस्राक्षीः न एताम् सृङ्काम् वित्त-मयीम् अवाप्तः यस्याम् मज्जन्ति बहवः मनुष्याः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: “You, O Naciketas, have reflected on the things men desire, the dear and the pleasing in form, and have let them go. You have not taken this path of wealth, in which many men sink.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the dear things are sons and the like, the pleasing ones the nymphs and the rest; Naciketas let them go on seeing that they pass away and have no substance. sṛṅkā here is a base path, trodden by the foolish. (At 1.1.16 he explained the same word as a necklace.)

sanskrit.deva:
दूरमेते विपरीते विषूची अविद्या या च विद्येति ज्ञाता ।
विद्याभीप्सिनं नचिकेतसं मन्ये न त्वा कामा बहवोऽलोलुपन्त ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
dūram ete viparīte viṣūcī avidyā yā ca vidyeti jñātā |
vidyābhīpsinaṃ naciketasaṃ manye na tvā kāmā bahavo 'lolupanta || 4 ||

lines.iast: dūram ete viparīte viṣūcī avidyā yā ca vidyeti jñātā
lines.deva: दूरमेते विपरीते विषूची अविद्या या च विद्येति ज्ञाता

lines.iast: vidyābhīpsinaṃ naciketasaṃ manye na tvā kāmā bahavo 'lolupanta
lines.deva: विद्याभीप्सिनं नचिकेतसं मन्ये न त्वा कामा बहवोऽलोलुपन्त

padaccheda.iast: dūram ete viparīte viṣūcī avidyā yā ca vidyā iti jñātā vidyā-abhīpsinam naciketasam manye na tvā kāmāḥ bahavaḥ alolupanta
padaccheda.deva: दूरम् एते विपरीते विषूची अविद्या या च विद्या इति ज्ञाता विद्या-अभीप्सिनम् नचिकेतसम् मन्ये न त्वा कामाः बहवः अलोलुपन्त

grammar.en: past passive participle f. nom. sg.

translations.text: “Far apart, opposed, and leading different ways are these two: ignorance, and what is known as knowledge. I consider Naciketas one who longs for knowledge, for the many desires did not tear you away.”

notes: Śaṅkara: they differ as darkness and light; one leads to the cycle of birth and death, the other to liberation. Ignorance has the pleasant for its object, knowledge the good. alolupanta: the desires did not cut Naciketas off from the path of the good.

sanskrit.deva:
अविद्यायामन्तरे वर्तमानाः स्वयं धीराः पण्डितं मन्यमानाः ।
दन्द्रम्यमाणाः परियन्ति मूढा अन्धेनैव नीयमाना यथान्धाः ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
avidyāyām antare vartamānāḥ svayaṃ dhīrāḥ paṇḍitaṃ manyamānāḥ |
dandramyamāṇāḥ pariyanti mūḍhā andhenaiva nīyamānā yathāndhāḥ || 5 ||

lines.iast: avidyāyām antare vartamānāḥ svayaṃ dhīrāḥ paṇḍitaṃ manyamānāḥ
lines.deva: अविद्यायामन्तरे वर्तमानाः स्वयं धीराः पण्डितं मन्यमानाः

lines.iast: dandramyamāṇāḥ pariyanti mūḍhā andhenaiva nīyamānā yathāndhāḥ
lines.deva: दन्द्रम्यमाणाः परियन्ति मूढा अन्धेनैव नीयमाना यथान्धाः

padaccheda.iast: avidyāyām antare vartamānāḥ svayam dhīrāḥ paṇḍitam manyamānāḥ dandramyamāṇāḥ pariyanti mūḍhāḥ andhena eva nīyamānāḥ yathā andhāḥ
padaccheda.deva: अविद्यायाम् अन्तरे वर्तमानाः स्वयम् धीराः पण्डितम् मन्यमानाः दन्द्रम्यमाणाः परियन्ति मूढाः अन्धेन एव नीयमानाः यथा अन्धाः

translations.text: “Living in the midst of ignorance, yet thinking themselves wise and learned, the deluded go round and round, staggering to and fro, like the blind led by one who is himself blind.”

notes: Śaṅkara: wrapped in hundreds of snares of craving for sons, cattle and the like, they follow a crooked course through the sufferings of old age, death and disease.
The DCS has the word dandramyamāṇāḥ in its text but gives no analysis for it; the analysis here is ours.

sanskrit.deva:
न साम्परायः प्रतिभाति बालं प्रमाद्यन्तं वित्तमोहेन मूढम् ।
अयं लोको नास्ति पर इति मानी पुनः पुनर्वशमापद्यते मे ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na sāmparāyaḥ pratibhāti bālaṃ pramādyantaṃ vittamohena mūḍham |
ayaṃ loko nāsti para iti mānī punaḥ punar vaśam āpadyate me || 6 ||

lines.iast: na sāmparāyaḥ pratibhāti bālaṃ pramādyantaṃ vittamohena mūḍham
lines.deva: न साम्परायः प्रतिभाति बालं प्रमाद्यन्तं वित्तमोहेन मूढम्

lines.iast: ayaṃ loko nāsti para iti mānī punaḥ punar vaśam āpadyate me
lines.deva: अयं लोको नास्ति पर इति मानी पुनः पुनर्वशमापद्यते मे

padaccheda.iast: na sāmparāyaḥ pratibhāti bālam pramādyantam vitta-mohena mūḍham ayam lokaḥ na asti paraḥ iti mānī punaḥ punaḥ vaśam āpadyate me
padaccheda.deva: न साम्परायः प्रतिभाति बालम् प्रमाद्यन्तम् वित्त-मोहेन मूढम् अयम् लोकः न अस्ति परः इति मानी पुनः पुनः वशम् आपद्यते मे

grammar.en: past passive participle m. acc. sg.

translations.text: “The passing beyond does not show itself to the childish one, heedless and deluded by the delusion of wealth. Thinking ‘there is this world and no other’, he falls under my sway again and again.”

notes: Śaṅkara: sāmparāya is the other world, and the scriptural means of reaching it. Such a man is born again and again and remains caught in the unbroken run of suffering that is birth and death. Most people are like this.

sanskrit.deva:
श्रवणायापि बहुभिर्यो न लभ्यः शृण्वन्तोऽपि बहवो यं न विद्युः ।
आश्चर्यो वक्ता कुशलोऽस्य लब्धा आश्चर्यो ज्ञाता कुशलानुशिष्टः ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śravaṇāyāpi bahubhir yo na labhyaḥ śṛṇvanto 'pi bahavo yaṃ na vidyuḥ |
āścaryo vaktā kuśalo 'sya labdhā āścaryo jñātā kuśalānuśiṣṭaḥ || 7 ||

lines.iast: śravaṇāyāpi bahubhir yo na labhyaḥ śṛṇvanto 'pi bahavo yaṃ na vidyuḥ
lines.deva: श्रवणायापि बहुभिर्यो न लभ्यः शृण्वन्तोऽपि बहवो यं न विद्युः

lines.iast: āścaryo vaktā kuśalo 'sya labdhā āścaryo jñātā kuśalānuśiṣṭaḥ
lines.deva: आश्चर्यो वक्ता कुशलोऽस्य लब्धा आश्चर्यो ज्ञाता कुशलानुशिष्टः

padaccheda.iast: śravaṇāya api bahubhiḥ yaḥ na labhyaḥ śṛṇvantaḥ api bahavaḥ yam na vidyuḥ āścaryaḥ vaktā kuśalaḥ asya labdhā āścaryaḥ jñātā kuśala-anuśiṣṭaḥ
padaccheda.deva: श्रवणाय अपि बहुभिः यः न लभ्यः शृण्वन्तः अपि बहवः यम् न विद्युः आश्चर्यः वक्ता कुशलः अस्य लब्धा आश्चर्यः ज्ञाता कुशल-अनुशिष्टः

translations.text: “He of whom many do not get even to hear, and whom many do not know even when they hear: a wonder is the one who teaches him, and skilful the one who attains him; a wonder is the one who knows him, taught by a skilful teacher.”

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘he’ is the Self. Among thousands, only one such as Naciketas seeks the good and comes to know the Self.

sanskrit.deva:
न नरेणावरेण प्रोक्त एष सुविज्ञेयो बहुधा चिन्त्यमानः ।
अनन्यप्रोक्ते गतिरत्र नास्त्यणीयान्ह्यतर्क्यमणुप्रमाणात् ॥ ८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na nareṇāvareṇa prokta eṣa suvijñeyo bahudhā cintyamānaḥ |
ananyaprokte gatir atra nāsty aṇīyān hy atarkyam aṇupramāṇāt || 8 ||

lines.iast: na nareṇāvareṇa prokta eṣa suvijñeyo bahudhā cintyamānaḥ
lines.deva: न नरेणावरेण प्रोक्त एष सुविज्ञेयो बहुधा चिन्त्यमानः

lines.iast: ananyaprokte gatir atra nāsty aṇīyān hy atarkyam aṇupramāṇāt
lines.deva: अनन्यप्रोक्ते गतिरत्र नास्त्यणीयान्ह्यतर्क्यमणुप्रमाणात्

padaccheda.iast: na nareṇa avareṇa proktaḥ eṣaḥ su-vijñeyaḥ bahudhā cintyamānaḥ an-anya-prokte gatiḥ atra na asti aṇīyān hi a-tarkyam aṇu-pramāṇāt
padaccheda.deva: न नरेण अवरेण प्रोक्तः एषः सु-विज्ञेयः बहुधा चिन्त्यमानः अन्-अन्य-प्रोक्ते गतिः अत्र न अस्ति अणीयान् हि अ-तर्क्यम् अणु-प्रमाणात्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

words.meaning: when taught by one who is not other
than what is of minute measure

translations.text: “Taught by an inferior man, this Self is not easy to understand well, for it is thought of in many ways. When it is taught by one who is not other than it, there is no more wavering about it; for it is subtler than the subtlest and beyond the reach of reasoning.”

notes: Śaṅkara: an inferior man is one of ordinary understanding. Disputants think of the Self variously: as existing or not, as agent or not, as pure or impure. ananyaprokte: taught by a teacher who sees no difference, who has become the Brahman he teaches.

Śaṅkara gives several senses for gatir atra nāsti: no more doubt of ‘is it or is it not’; nothing further left to be known; no more passage through birth and death; or, dividing the words as agatiḥ, no failure to understand.

sanskrit.deva:
नैषा तर्केण मतिरापनेया प्रोक्तान्येनैव सुज्ञानाय प्रेष्ठ ।
यां त्वमापः सत्यधृतिर्बतासि त्वादृङ्नो भूयान्नचिकेतः प्रष्टा ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
naiṣā tarkeṇa matir āpaneyā proktānyenaiva sujñānāya preṣṭha |
yāṃ tvam āpaḥ satyadhṛtir batāsi tvādṛṅ no bhūyān naciketaḥ praṣṭā || 9 ||

lines.iast: naiṣā tarkeṇa matir āpaneyā proktānyenaiva sujñānāya preṣṭha
lines.deva: नैषा तर्केण मतिरापनेया प्रोक्तान्येनैव सुज्ञानाय प्रेष्ठ

lines.iast: yāṃ tvam āpaḥ satyadhṛtir batāsi tvādṛṅ no bhūyān naciketaḥ praṣṭā
lines.deva: यां त्वमापः सत्यधृतिर्बतासि त्वादृङ्नो भूयान्नचिकेतः प्रष्टा

padaccheda.iast: na eṣā tarkeṇa matiḥ āpaneyā proktā anyena eva su-jñānāya preṣṭha yām tvam āpaḥ satya-dhṛtiḥ bata asi tvādṛk naḥ bhūyāt naciketaḥ praṣṭā
padaccheda.deva: न एषा तर्केण मतिः आपनेया प्रोक्ता अन्येन एव सु-ज्ञानाय प्रेष्ठ याम् त्वम् आपः सत्य-धृतिः बत असि त्वादृक् नः भूयात् नचिकेतः प्रष्टा

grammar.en: past passive participle f. nom. sg.

translations.text: “This understanding is not to be reached by reasoning. Taught by another, dearest one, it leads to sound knowledge. You have attained it. Ah, you are of true resolve! May we have a questioner like you, O Naciketas.”

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘another’ is a teacher versed in the scriptures, as distinct from a mere reasoner. āpaneyā: ‘to be reached’; or else ‘to be set aside’, in which case the sense is that this understanding is not to be given up for reasoning.
bhūyāt is a benedictive (āśīrliṅ); it is labelled here as an optative.

sanskrit.deva:
जानाम्यहं शेवधिरित्यनित्यं न ह्यध्रुवैः प्राप्यते हि ध्रुवं तत् ।
ततो मया नाचिकेतश्चितोऽग्निरनित्यैर्द्रव्यैः प्राप्तवानस्मि नित्यम् ॥ १० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
jānāmy ahaṃ śevadhir ity anityaṃ na hy adhruvaiḥ prāpyate hi dhruvaṃ tat |
tato mayā nāciketaś cito 'gnir anityair dravyaiḥ prāptavān asmi nityam || 10 ||

lines.iast: jānāmy ahaṃ śevadhir ity anityaṃ na hy adhruvaiḥ prāpyate hi dhruvaṃ tat
lines.deva: जानाम्यहं शेवधिरित्यनित्यं न ह्यध्रुवैः प्राप्यते हि ध्रुवं तत्

lines.iast: tato mayā nāciketaś cito 'gnir anityair dravyaiḥ prāptavān asmi nityam
lines.deva: ततो मया नाचिकेतश्चितोऽग्निरनित्यैर्द्रव्यैः प्राप्तवानस्मि नित्यम्

padaccheda.iast: jānāmi aham śevadhiḥ iti anityam na hi adhruvaiḥ prāpyate hi dhruvam tat tataḥ mayā nāciketaḥ citaḥ agniḥ anityaiḥ dravyaiḥ prāptavān asmi nityam
padaccheda.deva: जानामि अहम् शेवधिः इति अनित्यम् न हि अध्रुवैः प्राप्यते हि ध्रुवम् तत् ततः मया नाचिकेतः चितः अग्निः अनित्यैः द्रव्यैः प्राप्तवान् अस्मि नित्यम्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.
past active participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: “I know that what is called treasure is impermanent, for what is stable is not attained by things that are unstable. Therefore I built the Nāciketa fire with impermanent things, and I have attained what is lasting.”

notes: Śaṅkara: Yama, pleased, speaks again. The treasure is the fruit of rites. The ‘lasting’ that he gained is the station of Yama, called heaven, which lasts only in a relative sense; the truly stable treasure, the supreme Self, is not reached by such means.

sanskrit.deva:
कामस्य आप्तिं जगतः प्रतिष्ठां क्रतोरनन्त्यमभयस्य पारम् ।
स्तोममहदुरुगायं प्रतिष्ठां दृष्ट्वा धृत्या धीरो नचिकेतोऽत्यस्राक्षीः ॥ ११ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
kāmasya āptiṃ jagataḥ pratiṣṭhāṃ krator anantyam abhayasya pāram |
stomamahad urugāyaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ dṛṣṭvā dhṛtyā dhīro naciketo 'tyasrākṣīḥ || 11 ||

lines.iast: kāmasya āptiṃ jagataḥ pratiṣṭhāṃ krator anantyam abhayasya pāram
lines.deva: कामस्य आप्तिं जगतः प्रतिष्ठां क्रतोरनन्त्यमभयस्य पारम्

lines.iast: stomamahad urugāyaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ dṛṣṭvā dhṛtyā dhīro naciketo 'tyasrākṣīḥ
lines.deva: स्तोममहदुरुगायं प्रतिष्ठां दृष्ट्वा धृत्या धीरो नचिकेतोऽत्यस्राक्षीः

padaccheda.iast: kāmasya āptim jagataḥ pratiṣṭhām kratoḥ anantyam abhayasya pāram stoma-mahat uru-gāyam pratiṣṭhām dṛṣṭvā dhṛtyā dhīraḥ naciketaḥ atyasrākṣīḥ
padaccheda.deva: कामस्य आप्तिम् जगतः प्रतिष्ठाम् क्रतोः अनन्त्यम् अभयस्य पारम् स्तोम-महत् उरु-गायम् प्रतिष्ठाम् दृष्ट्वा धृत्या धीरः नचिकेतः अत्यस्राक्षीः

translations.text: “The fulfilment of desire, the support of the world, the endless fruit of meditation, the farther shore of fearlessness, great and worthy of praise, far-reaching, a firm standing: having seen all this, O Naciketas, you, being wise, have with firmness let it go.”

notes: Śaṅkara: all of this describes the state of Hiraṇyagarbha, the fruit of meditation (kratu here is upāsanā). Naciketas gave up even that, desiring only the highest.

sanskrit.deva:
तं दुर्दर्शं गूढमनुप्रविष्टं गुहाहितं गह्वरेष्ठं पुराणम् ।
अध्यात्मयोगाधिगमेन देवं मत्वा धीरो हर्षशोकौ जहाति ॥ १२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
taṃ durdarśaṃ gūḍham anupraviṣṭaṃ guhāhitaṃ gahvareṣṭhaṃ purāṇam |
adhyātmayogādhigamena devaṃ matvā dhīro harṣaśokau jahāti || 12 ||

lines.iast: taṃ durdarśaṃ gūḍham anupraviṣṭaṃ guhāhitaṃ gahvareṣṭhaṃ purāṇam
lines.deva: तं दुर्दर्शं गूढमनुप्रविष्टं गुहाहितं गह्वरेष्ठं पुराणम्

lines.iast: adhyātmayogādhigamena devaṃ matvā dhīro harṣaśokau jahāti
lines.deva: अध्यात्मयोगाधिगमेन देवं मत्वा धीरो हर्षशोकौ जहाति

padaccheda.iast: tam durdarśam gūḍham anupraviṣṭam guhā-hitam gahvareṣṭham purāṇam adhyātma-yoga-adhigamena devam matvā dhīraḥ harṣa-śokau jahāti
padaccheda.deva: तम् दुर्दर्शम् गूढम् अनुप्रविष्टम् गुहा-हितम् गह्वरेष्ठम् पुराणम् अध्यात्म-योग-अधिगमेन देवम् मत्वा धीरः हर्ष-शोकौ जहाति

grammar.en: past passive participle n. acc. sg.
past passive participle m. acc. sg.

words.meaning: by attaining concentration on the Self

translations.text: “Him who is hard to see, who has entered into what is hidden, who is set in the cave and dwells in the deep, the ancient one: knowing that shining one by fixing the mind on the Self, the wise man leaves joy and sorrow behind.”

notes: Śaṅkara: this is the Self that Naciketas wishes to know, hidden by the perceptions of ordinary objects. The cave is the intellect, where it is perceived; the ‘deep’ is a hard place crowded with many evils. adhyātmayoga: withdrawing the mind from objects and settling it on the Self. deva is the Self.

sanskrit.deva:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा सम्परिगृह्य मर्त्यः प्रवृह्य धर्म्यमणुमेतमाप्य ।
स मोदते मोदनीयं हि लब्ध्वा विवृतं सद्म नचिकेतसं मन्ये ॥ १३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
etacchrutvā samparigṛhya martyaḥ pravṛhya dharmyam aṇum etam āpya |
sa modate modanīyaṃ hi labdhvā vivṛtaṃ sadma naciketasaṃ manye || 13 ||

lines.iast: etacchrutvā samparigṛhya martyaḥ pravṛhya dharmyam aṇum etam āpya
lines.deva: एतच्छ्रुत्वा सम्परिगृह्य मर्त्यः प्रवृह्य धर्म्यमणुमेतमाप्य

lines.iast: sa modate modanīyaṃ hi labdhvā vivṛtaṃ sadma naciketasaṃ manye
lines.deva: स मोदते मोदनीयं हि लब्ध्वा विवृतं सद्म नचिकेतसं मन्ये

padaccheda.iast: etat śrutvā samparigṛhya martyaḥ pravṛhya dharmyam aṇum etam āpya saḥ modate modanīyam hi labdhvā vivṛtam sadma naciketasam manye
padaccheda.deva: एतत् श्रुत्वा सम्परिगृह्य मर्त्यः प्रवृह्य धर्म्यम् अणुम् एतम् आप्य सः मोदते मोदनीयम् हि लब्ध्वा विवृतम् सद्म नचिकेतसम् मन्ये

grammar.en: past passive participle n. acc. sg.

translations.text: “Having heard this and grasped it fully, having drawn out this subtle Self, which accords with dharma, and attained it, the mortal rejoices, for he has gained what is worth rejoicing in. The abode, I think, stands open for Naciketas.”

notes: Śaṅkara: pravṛhya: setting the Self apart from the body and the rest. The abode is Brahman, its door open to Naciketas: ‘I consider you fit for liberation.’

sanskrit.deva:
अन्यत्र धर्मादन्यत्राधर्मादन्यत्रास्मात्कृताकृतात् ।
अन्यत्र भूताच्च भव्याच्च यत्तत्पश्यसि तद्वद ॥ १४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
anyatra dharmād anyatrādharmād anyatrāsmāt kṛtākṛtāt |
anyatra bhūtāc ca bhavyāc ca yat tat paśyasi tad vada || 14 ||

lines.iast: anyatra dharmād anyatrādharmād anyatrāsmāt kṛtākṛtāt
lines.deva: अन्यत्र धर्मादन्यत्राधर्मादन्यत्रास्मात्कृताकृतात्

lines.iast: anyatra bhūtāc ca bhavyāc ca yat tat paśyasi tad vada
lines.deva: अन्यत्र भूताच्च भव्याच्च यत्तत्पश्यसि तद्वद

padaccheda.iast: anyatra dharmāt anyatra adharmāt anyatra asmāt kṛta-akṛtāt anyatra bhūtāt ca bhavyāt ca yat tat paśyasi tat vada
padaccheda.deva: अन्यत्र धर्मात् अन्यत्र अधर्मात् अन्यत्र अस्मात् कृत-अकृतात् अन्यत्र भूतात् च भव्यात् च यत् तत् पश्यसि तत् वद

translations.text: “That which you see as apart from righteousness and apart from unrighteousness, apart from this effect and cause, apart from what has been and what is to be: tell me that.”

notes: Śaṅkara: Naciketas speaks. dharma is the doing of what scripture enjoins, with its results and its means; kṛta is the effect and akṛta the cause. With past and future the present too is meant: that which the three times do not limit.

sanskrit.deva:
सर्वे वेदा यत्पदमामनन्ति तपांसि सर्वाणि च यद्वदन्ति ।
यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति तत्ते पदं संग्रहेण ब्रवीमि ओमित्येतत् ॥ १५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sarve vedā yat padam āmananti tapāṃsi sarvāṇi ca yad vadanti |
yad icchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti tat te padaṃ saṃgraheṇa bravīmi om ity etat || 15 ||

lines.iast: sarve vedā yat padam āmananti tapāṃsi sarvāṇi ca yad vadanti
lines.deva: सर्वे वेदा यत्पदमामनन्ति तपांसि सर्वाणि च यद्वदन्ति

lines.iast: yad icchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti tat te padaṃ saṃgraheṇa bravīmi om ity etat
lines.deva: यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति तत्ते पदं संग्रहेण ब्रवीमि ओमित्येतत्

padaccheda.iast: sarve vedāḥ yat padam āmananti tapāṃsi sarvāṇi ca yat vadanti yat icchantaḥ brahmacaryam caranti tat te padam saṃgraheṇa bravīmi om iti etat
padaccheda.deva: सर्वे वेदाः यत् पदम् आमनन्ति तपांसि सर्वाणि च यत् वदन्ति यत् इच्छन्तः ब्रह्मचर्यम् चरन्ति तत् ते पदम् संग्रहेण ब्रवीमि ॐ इति एतत्

words.meaning: the life of a religious student

translations.text: “The goal that all the Vedas declare, that all austerities speak of, and desiring which people live the life of a religious student: that goal I tell you in brief. It is this: Om.”

notes: The DCS sets “om ity etat” apart as a verse of its own and leaves bravīmi unjoined. Śaṅkara's text and the common editions keep the words in this verse, reading bravīmy om ity etat.
Śaṅkara: Death speaks. pada is ‘that which is to be reached’. Austerities ‘speak of’ it in that they are means of attaining it. Om is both the word that denotes it and its symbol.

sanskrit.deva:
एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं ब्रह्म एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं परम् ।
एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं ज्ञात्वा यो यदिच्छति तस्य तत् ॥ १६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
etaddhy evākṣaraṃ brahma etaddhyevākṣaraṃ param |
etaddhyevākṣaraṃ jñātvā yo yad icchati tasya tat || 16 ||

lines.iast: etaddhy evākṣaraṃ brahma etaddhyevākṣaraṃ param
lines.deva: एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं ब्रह्म एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं परम्

lines.iast: etaddhyevākṣaraṃ jñātvā yo yad icchati tasya tat
lines.deva: एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं ज्ञात्वा यो यदिच्छति तस्य तत्

padaccheda.iast: etat hi eva akṣaram brahma etat hi eva akṣaram param etat hi eva akṣaram jñātvā yaḥ yat icchati tasya tat
padaccheda.deva: एतत् हि एव अक्षरम् ब्रह्म एतत् हि एव अक्षरम् परम् एतत् हि एव अक्षरम् ज्ञात्वा यः यत् इच्छति तस्य तत्

translations.text: “This syllable indeed is Brahman; this syllable indeed is the supreme. Knowing this very syllable, whatever one desires is his.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the first ‘Brahman’ is the lower Brahman and ‘the supreme’ the higher; the syllable is the symbol of both. One who meditates on it as Brahman gains whichever he seeks: the higher is to be known, the lower to be attained.

sanskrit.deva:
एतदालम्बनं श्रेष्ठमेतदालम्बनं परम् ।
एतदालम्बनं ज्ञात्वा ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥ १७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
etad ālambanaṃ śreṣṭham etad ālambanaṃ param |
etad ālambanaṃ jñātvā brahmaloke mahīyate || 17 ||

lines.iast: etad ālambanaṃ śreṣṭham etad ālambanaṃ param
lines.deva: एतदालम्बनं श्रेष्ठमेतदालम्बनं परम्

lines.iast: etad ālambanaṃ jñātvā brahmaloke mahīyate
lines.deva: एतदालम्बनं ज्ञात्वा ब्रह्मलोके महीयते

padaccheda.iast: etat ālambanam śreṣṭham etat ālambanam param etat ālambanam jñātvā brahma-loke mahīyate
padaccheda.deva: एतत् आलम्बनम् श्रेष्ठम् एतत् आलम्बनम् परम् एतत् आलम्बनम् ज्ञात्वा ब्रह्म-लोके महीयते

translations.text: “This support is the best; this support is the highest. Knowing this support, one is honoured in the world of Brahman.”

notes: Śaṅkara: it is the best of the supports for attaining Brahman, and relates to both the higher and the lower Brahman. ‘Honoured in the world of Brahman’: having become Brahman, he is to be revered as Brahman.

sanskrit.deva:
न जायते म्रियते वा विपश्चिन्नायं कुतश्चिन्न बभूव कश्चित् ।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥ १८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścin nāyaṃ kutaścin na babhūva kaścit |
ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre || 18 ||

lines.iast: na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścin nāyaṃ kutaścin na babhūva kaścit
lines.deva: न जायते म्रियते वा विपश्चिन्नायं कुतश्चिन्न बभूव कश्चित्

lines.iast: ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre
lines.deva: अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे

padaccheda.iast: na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścit na ayam kutaścit na babhūva kaścit ajaḥ nityaḥ śāśvataḥ ayam purāṇaḥ na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre
padaccheda.deva: न जायते म्रियते वा विपश्चित् न अयम् कुतश्चित् न बभूव कश्चित् अजः नित्यः शाश्वतः अयम् पुराणः न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे

translations.text: “The knowing Self is not born, nor does it die. It did not come from anything, nor did anything come from it. Unborn, eternal, everlasting and ancient, it is not slain when the body is slain.”

notes: Śaṅkara: vipaścit, ‘intelligent’, because its nature as consciousness is never lost. Birth and death, the first and last of the changes that belong to things that arise, are denied so as to deny all change. purāṇa: ‘new even of old’, that is, without growth. It is in the body as space is.

sanskrit.deva:
हन्ता चेन्मन्यते हन्तुं हतश्चेन्मन्यते हतम् ।
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते ॥ १९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
hantā cen manyate hantuṃ hataś cen manyate hatam |
ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate || 19 ||

lines.iast: hantā cen manyate hantuṃ hataś cen manyate hatam
lines.deva: हन्ता चेन्मन्यते हन्तुं हतश्चेन्मन्यते हतम्

lines.iast: ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate
lines.deva: उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते

padaccheda.iast: hantā cet manyate hantum hataḥ cet manyate hatam ubhau tau na vijānītaḥ na ayam hanti na hanyate
padaccheda.deva: हन्ता चेत् मन्यते हन्तुम् हतः चेत् मन्यते हतम् उभौ तौ न विजानीतः न अयम् हन्ति न हन्यते

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.
past passive participle m. acc. sg.

translations.text: “If the slayer thinks that he slays, and if the slain thinks himself slain, neither of the two knows. This Self does not slay, nor is it slain.”

notes: Śaṅkara: both take the body alone to be the Self. The cycle of birth and death, with its merit and demerit, belongs only to one who does not know the Self.

sanskrit.deva:
अणोरणीयान्महतो महीयानात्मास्य जन्तोर्निहितो गुहायाम् ।
तमक्रतुः पश्यति वीतशोको धातुप्रसादान्महिमानमात्मनः ॥ २० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
aṇor aṇīyān mahato mahīyān ātmāsya jantor nihito guhāyām |
tam akratuḥ paśyati vītaśoko dhātuprasādān mahimānam ātmanaḥ || 20 ||

lines.iast: aṇor aṇīyān mahato mahīyān ātmāsya jantor nihito guhāyām
lines.deva: अणोरणीयान्महतो महीयानात्मास्य जन्तोर्निहितो गुहायाम्

lines.iast: tam akratuḥ paśyati vītaśoko dhātuprasādān mahimānam ātmanaḥ
lines.deva: तमक्रतुः पश्यति वीतशोको धातुप्रसादान्महिमानमात्मनः

padaccheda.iast: aṇoḥ aṇīyān mahataḥ mahīyān ātmā asya jantoḥ nihitaḥ guhāyām tam akratuḥ paśyati vīta-śokaḥ dhātu-prasādāt mahimānam ātmanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अणोः अणीयान् महतः महीयान् आत्मा अस्य जन्तोः निहितः गुहायाम् तम् अक्रतुः पश्यति वीत-शोकः धातु-प्रसादात् महिमानम् आत्मनः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

words.meaning: through the serenity of the organs

translations.text: “Subtler than the subtle, greater than the great, the Self is set in the cave of the heart of this creature. One who is free from desire sees that greatness of the Self through the serenity of the mind and senses, and becomes free from sorrow.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the cave is the heart, of every creature from Brahmā down to a tuft of grass. akratu: without desire, the mind withdrawn from outer objects, seen and unseen. The dhātus are the mind and the other organs, so called because they sustain the body. The greatness of the Self neither grows nor declines through action; he sees it directly, as ‘I am this’.

sanskrit.deva:
आसीनो दूरं व्रजति शयानो याति सर्वतः ।
कस्तं मदामदं देवं मदन्यो ज्ञातुमर्हति ॥ २१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
āsīno dūraṃ vrajati śayāno yāti sarvataḥ |
kas taṃ madāmadaṃ devaṃ mad anyo jñātum arhati || 21 ||

lines.iast: āsīno dūraṃ vrajati śayāno yāti sarvataḥ
lines.deva: आसीनो दूरं व्रजति शयानो याति सर्वतः

lines.iast: kas taṃ madāmadaṃ devaṃ mad anyo jñātum arhati
lines.deva: कस्तं मदामदं देवं मदन्यो ज्ञातुमर्हति

padaccheda.iast: āsīnaḥ dūram vrajati śayānaḥ yāti sarvataḥ kaḥ tam madāmadam devam mat anyaḥ jñātum arhati
padaccheda.deva: आसीनः दूरम् व्रजति शयानः याति सर्वतः कः तम् मदामदम् देवम् मत् अन्यः ज्ञातुम् अर्हति

words.meaning: who rejoices and does not rejoice

translations.text: “Sitting, it travels far; lying down, it goes everywhere. Who other than I can know that shining one, who both rejoices and does not rejoice?”

notes: Śaṅkara: because of its limiting adjuncts the Self seems to have opposed qualities, rest and movement, joy and its absence, as a jewel shows many colours. So it is hard to know, except for one of subtle understanding such as Yama. ‘Lying down’: when the organs are at rest and particular cognition has ceased.

sanskrit.deva:
अशरीरं शरीरेषु अनवस्थेष्ववस्थितम् ।
महान्तं विभुमात्मानं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति ॥ २२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
aśarīraṃ śarīreṣu anavastheṣv avasthitam |
mahāntaṃ vibhum ātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati || 22 ||

lines.iast: aśarīraṃ śarīreṣu anavastheṣv avasthitam
lines.deva: अशरीरं शरीरेषु अनवस्थेष्ववस्थितम्

lines.iast: mahāntaṃ vibhum ātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati
lines.deva: महान्तं विभुमात्मानं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति

padaccheda.iast: aśarīram śarīreṣu anavastheṣu avasthitam mahāntam vibhum ātmānam matvā dhīraḥ na śocati
padaccheda.deva: अशरीरम् शरीरेषु अनवस्थेषु अवस्थितम् महान्तम् विभुम् आत्मानम् मत्वा धीरः न शोचति

grammar.en: past passive participle m. acc. sg.

translations.text: “Knowing the Self as bodiless within bodies, abiding within what does not abide, great and all-pervading, the wise man does not grieve.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the bodies are those of gods, ancestors, men and the rest, all impermanent. The word ātman shows that it is not other than oneself: he knows it as ‘I am this’.

sanskrit.deva:
नायमात्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यो न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन ।
यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्यस्तस्यैष आत्मा विवृणुते तनूं स्वाम् ॥ २३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
nāyam ātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā na bahunā śrutena |
yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṃ svām || 23 ||

lines.iast: nāyam ātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā na bahunā śrutena
lines.deva: नायमात्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यो न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन

lines.iast: yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṃ svām
lines.deva: यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्यस्तस्यैष आत्मा विवृणुते तनूं स्वाम्

padaccheda.iast: na ayam ātmā pravacanena labhyaḥ na medhayā na bahunā śrutena yam eva eṣaḥ vṛṇute tena labhyaḥ tasya eṣaḥ ātmā vivṛṇute tanūm svām
padaccheda.deva: न अयम् आत्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यः न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन यम् एव एषः वृणुते तेन लभ्यः तस्य एषः आत्मा विवृणुते तनूम् स्वाम्

translations.text: “This Self is not attained by study of the Vedas, nor by intellect, nor by much learning. It is attained through the very Self that the seeker longs for; to him this Self reveals its own nature.”

notes: Śaṅkara: pravacana: mastering many Vedas; medhā: the power to retain the meaning of texts. The Self that this seeker prays for is attained through that same Self: one who, free from desire, seeks the Self alone, gains the Self by the Self. tanū: its true nature.

sanskrit.deva:
नाविरतो दुश्चरितान्नाशान्तो नासमाहितः ।
नाशान्तमानसो वापि प्रज्ञानेनैनमाप्नुयात् ॥ २४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
nāvirato duścaritān nāśānto nāsamāhitaḥ |
nāśāntamānaso vāpi prajñānenainam āpnuyāt || 24 ||

lines.iast: nāvirato duścaritān nāśānto nāsamāhitaḥ
lines.deva: नाविरतो दुश्चरितान्नाशान्तो नासमाहितः

lines.iast: nāśāntamānaso vāpi prajñānenainam āpnuyāt
lines.deva: नाशान्तमानसो वापि प्रज्ञानेनैनमाप्नुयात्

padaccheda.iast: na a-virataḥ duścaritāt na a-śāntaḥ na a-samāhitaḥ na a-śānta-mānasaḥ vā api prajñānena enam āpnuyāt
padaccheda.deva: न अ-विरतः दुश्चरितात् न अ-शान्तः न अ-समाहितः न अ-शान्त-मानसः वा अपि प्रज्ञानेन एनम् आप्नुयात्

words.meaning: one who has not turned away
one whose mind is not at peace

translations.text: “One who has not turned away from bad conduct, who is not calm, who is not concentrated, or whose mind is not at peace, cannot attain this Self by knowledge.”

notes: Śaṅkara: aśānta: not withdrawn from the restlessness of the senses; asamāhita: with a scattered mind; aśāntamānasa: one whose mind, though concentrated, is still busy seeking the fruits of concentration. One free of these, who has a teacher, attains the Self through the knowledge of Brahman.

sanskrit.deva:
यस्य ब्रह्म च क्षत्रं च उभे भवत ओदनः ।
मृत्युर्यस्योपसेचनं क इत्था वेद यत्र सः ॥ २५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yasya brahma ca kṣatraṃ ca ubhe bhavata odanaḥ |
mṛtyur yasyopasecanaṃ ka itthā veda yatra saḥ || 25 ||

lines.iast: yasya brahma ca kṣatraṃ ca ubhe bhavata odanaḥ
lines.deva: यस्य ब्रह्म च क्षत्रं च उभे भवत ओदनः

lines.iast: mṛtyur yasyopasecanaṃ ka itthā veda yatra saḥ
lines.deva: मृत्युर्यस्योपसेचनं क इत्था वेद यत्र सः

padaccheda.iast: yasya brahma ca kṣatram ca ubhe bhavataḥ odanaḥ mṛtyuḥ yasya upasecanam kaḥ itthā veda yatra saḥ
padaccheda.deva: यस्य ब्रह्म च क्षत्रम् च उभे भवतः ओदनः मृत्युः यस्य उपसेचनम् कः इत्था वेद यत्र सः

translations.text: “He for whom the brahmin and the warrior orders are both food, and death the sauce upon it: who thus knows where he is?”

notes: Śaṅkara: a man of ordinary understanding, without the means just described, cannot know the Self as one who has them does. Brahmin and warrior, upholders of all order and protectors of all, are mere food to it, and Death, who carries off everything, does not even suffice as its sauce.
